text:
maria: Heads up — since the 02:00 deploy prod services intermittently fail DNS for internal hostnames (e.g. redis.service.prod.svc.cluster.local). Some pods resolve to public IPs instead of the cluster IP and connections time out.
raj: any pattern on node/zone?
maria: mostly eu-west nodes, but a few in us-west. Failures spike around bursty job starts.
sam: can you paste a failing `getent hosts redis.service.prod.svc.cluster.local` from an affected pod?
maria: here (from a crashlooping worker):
```
$ getent hosts redis.service.prod.svc.cluster.local
10.11.2.9 redis.service.prod.svc.cluster.local
93.184.216.34 redis.service.prod.svc.cluster.local
```
liz: whoa — that's picking up an external IP after the cluster IP. Do we have `files` or `/etc/hosts` entries being added? check `nsswitch.conf` on the node.
maria: node shows `hosts: files mdns4_minimal [NOTFOUND=return] dns myhostname`
so files first.
raj: any recent configmanagement change that writes /etc/hosts? deploy-bot, did the hostfile role run in the 02:00 window?
deploy-bot: config-run: hostfile-updates.yml applied to 12 nodes at 02:03 UTC. Changed entries: added fqdn aliases for a legacy monitoring endpoint.
sam: that would explain it — `files` before `dns` means /etc/hosts wins. How did the external domain get mapped to the internal name though? sounds like hostfile entries used short names and search path expansion hit external hostname.
maria: digging: the template added entries like `93.184.216.34 redis.service.prod` (no .svc.cluster.local). With kube DNS search path `redis.service.prod` expands to `redis.service.prod.svc.cluster.local` because of ndots/search, so hosts file mapping matched first.
liz: aha — hostfile entries with unqualified names + cluster search path produced collisions. We mostly rely on split-horizon DNS; files should not shadow cluster names.
raj: mitigation options: 1) remove offending /etc/hosts entries 2) change nsswitch to `dns` before `files` (risky) 3) add fully-qualified entries in hostfile explicitly pointing to cluster IPs 4) patch templating to avoid short names.
sam: quick fix: remove the legacy hostfile role from the 12 affected nodes and reload resolv cache: `sudo systemctl restart systemd-resolved` + flush node-local-dns cache: `kubectl -n kube-system exec daemonset/node-local-dns -- pumba netns --` (or just restart the daemonset pod).
maria: I'm removing entries now on a canary node and restarting node-local-dns. Will report.
oncall-bot: incident-ticket created: INC-2026-1840123 — priority P2 — assign eng-infra.
liz: longer term we should: a) change CM template to use FQDNs for hostfile entries, b) add a CI lint that fails if hostfile contains names that match `.svc.cluster.local`, c) add a k8s admission webhook to detect pods with hostAliases?
raj: agree. Also add a warning in deployment playbook about `hosts: files` ordering consequences with cluster search path/ndots.
sam: can we also search other clusters for the same CM change? run: `repo:infra-config path:roles/hostfile` and grep for unqualified names.
maria: can confirm removing entries restored correct resolution on canary. I'm rolling removal to remaining 11 nodes now. Will watch metrics for 15m.
maria: update — after removals all pods on the canary node resolve to cluster IP and latencies dropped back to normal :thumbsup:
